identity.name: Hyeonse Im
identity.headline: Frontend engineer building customer web and WebView experiences and operations tools, with a role in technical decisions
identity.introduction: Since March 2022, I have built customer websites, WebViews, and operations tools for SWING, SWAP, and Yellow Bus at The SWING. My work spans early service development, login and payment flows, app integration, rebuilding acquired services, and web performance. Since September 2025, I have served as SWAP FE Part Lead, working on major features, technical decisions, and code reviews within SWAP FE.

featuredCases.title: Connecting Bike operations across staff admin and business portal screens
featuredCases.period: 2026 · Major API integration in June / business portal in July
featuredCases.role: Responsible for the project's frontend work
featuredCases.context: First orders, contract delivery, vehicle handover, insurance changes, and payment history spanned staff operations and the business customer's experience. Existing operations continued while the new system was being built.
approach: I separated the staff flow for creating a first order and sending a contract in Admin from the business customer's flow for viewing payment history and schedules in My Page.

Before the APIs were finalized, I used fixtures in a nonproduction environment to check return, handover, and insurance change screens, and documented the needed APIs, fields, and replacement targets.
I adjusted screens and permission-based navigation for each user type, along with vehicle, store, and insurance request fields, to match the actual response contract.
featuredCases.verification: After Playwright E2E tests, I inspected the screens and found a B2C response missing the business information object, leaving fields blank. After a backend response change and a frontend condition fix, I repeated automated and manual checks.
featuredCases.outcome: Implemented staff order and contract flows and self-service lookup screens for business customers, and checked the workflows before and after the APIs were finalized.
featuredCases.boundary: The backend owned migration of existing data. I do not present a measured reduction in manual work or costs.

featuredCases.title: Contributing to the SWAP Admin V1 to V2 transition
featuredCases.role: SWAP FE development and technical review
featuredCases.context: The existing task lookup path remained in use as V2 subscription, task, and factoring screens and APIs were introduced.
approach: I worked on connecting V2 subscription, task, and factoring screens to the Fleet API.
I contributed to navigation based on data version and to the transition of related operations features.
I worked on permissions and sidebar navigation to connect the existing Admin and V2 screens.
featuredCases.verification: The December 2025 Admin V2 release included subscription, task, and factoring screens integrated with the Fleet API. At the time, task details used V2 lookup first with a V1 fallback path.
featuredCases.outcome: Contributed to the Admin V2 screen and API transition while old and new task data coexisted.
featuredCases.boundary: This describes the transition of SWAP's operations Admin. I describe the lookup path used at the time without claiming a measured error rate or completion of the entire service migration.

featuredCases.title: Rebuilding Yellow Bus legacy operations in a new Admin
featuredCases.role: Frontend engineer in the Yellow Bus squad
featuredCases.context: The acquired school shuttle service had several operations tools built with PHP, JavaScript, and React. Internal staff and academies used different functions and permissions.
approach: I mapped existing student, dispatch, route, and manager functions and moved them into a React and TypeScript Admin.
I organized staff and academy permissions and student–academy relationships, then built dispatch, boarding status, and pickup and drop-off stop changes.
I developed bus monitoring, Kakao Map route and stop management, schedule printing, and operator guides.
featuredCases.verification: I connected academy-specific dispatch lookup, mapped routes, boarding status and stop changes, and access limits in the new operations screens. I also coordinated exceptional student records and the response contract with backend colleagues.
featuredCases.outcome: Rebuilt distributed operations functions into workflows in the new Admin and contributed to initial stabilization.
featuredCases.boundary: The focus is on rebuilding workflows and features. I do not claim a completion date for the entire migration or a measured stabilization effect.

featuredCases.title: Reducing first-screen display delay and transferred assets
featuredCases.role: Frontend development for the SWING website
featuredCases.context: The initial rendering approach and large media, fonts, and external content delayed display of the first screen.
approach: I moved from the Next.js Pages Router to an App Router structure that favors server rendering, and prerendered Korean and English routes.
I replaced the hero GIF with an MP4 and WebP poster, delayed external content, and selected a variable WOFF2 subset that preserved the design's font weights.
To address the first image conversion delay found in production, I later generated 106 responsive WebP assets from 34 originals at build time.
featuredCases.verification: I compared medians from three before and five after Lighthouse mobile simulation runs under the same local production-build conditions.
featuredCases.outcome: Recorded a Performance score change from 54 to 95 and initial transfer size from 19.805 to 0.488 MB (a 97.5% reduction).
featuredCases.boundary: These are local simulation results, not real-user performance or conversion metrics. Several changes were applied together.
